title.narrative: Emergency Food and Recovery Assistance for the 2024 Bangladesh Eastern Flood Response

description.narrative: The latest wave of flash floods in Eastern Bangladesh, driven by heavy rainfall and upstream water flows from India, has severely affected 11 districts in the Sylhet and Chattogram divisions, with Cumilla, Feni, Noakhali, Lakshmipur, and Moulvibazar among the hardest hit. The floods have impacted over 5.8 million people, displacing more than 500,000 and leaving over a million stranded. Floodwaters have submerged rural roads, agricultural fields, and fishponds, devastating crops and other vital livelihoods crucial to the local economy and food security. A Key Immediate Needs and Situation Analysis by the Needs Assessment Working Group (NAWG) has identified approximately 1.7 million people facing food insecurity, urgently needing life-saving food assistance.In response to the flash floods, WFP has developed a three-phase plan, beginning with the immediate distribution of fortified biscuits in the districts of Cumilla, Feni, Noakhali, Lakshmipur, and Maulvibazar. This will be followed by multi-purpose cash assistance and cash-for-work programs, prioritizing the five districts of Cumilla, Feni, Noakhali, Lakshmipur, and Moulvibazar.As part of the initial phase, with funds from CERF and other sources, WFP already completed the provision of 607MT of fortified biscuits to 120,782 households as an immediate food assistance. Each household received 5kg of fortified rice When water receded to an optimal level and markets returned to its regular functionality, WFP began the second phase of response through unconditional cash assistance. In total, WFP targets 166,000 households in the five most affected districts with each household receiving BDT 6,000 (equivalent to US$50) for two distribution cycles, enabling them to meet daily food and other essential needs. As part of the third phase, cash-for-work interventions will be conducted to restore livelihood and damaged infrastructure.Out of the overall response plan, WFP will implement the following activities in four districts - Feni, Cumilla, Nohakhali and Lakshmipur with the support of the CERF fund specifically: • 1st phase: CERF funding will cover 150MT of fortified biscuits already distributed to 30,000 households (150,000 people).• 2nd phase: WFP will provide unconditional cash (BDT6000) to 26,800 households (128,925 people) for one month.• 3rd phase: Of the people assisted under the second phase, 1,015 households (5,075 people) will receive BDT 500 per day for 20 working days in one cycle distribution (or BDT 10,000) as compensation for their work on infrastructure reconstruction.Throughout the response, awareness messages on food and nutrition and other essential needs particularly on safe drinking water consumption, WASH (in coordination with UNICEF), Protection, Gender based violence (GBV), community feedback mechanism (CFM), financial literacy, and entitlement will be also disseminated to the affected population through SMS and household visits.
